116: *  3DMO m3dchunk_t file header chunk, may followed by compressed data
117: *  HEAD m3dhdr_t model header chunk
118: *  n x m3dchunk_t more chunks follow
119- *      PRVW preview chunk (optional)
120- *      CMAP color map chunk (optional)
121- *      TMAP texture map chunk (optional)
122- *      VRTS vertex data chunk (optional if it's a material library)
123- *      BONE bind-pose skeleton, bone hierarchy chunk (optional)
124- *          n x m3db_t contains propably more, but at least one bone
125- *          n x m3ds_t skin group records
126- *      MTRL* material chunk(s), can be more (optional)
127- *          n x m3dp_t each material contains propapbly more, but at least one property
128- *                     the properties are configurable with a static array, see m3d_propertytypes
129: *      n x m3dchunk_t at least one, but maybe more face chunks
130- *          PROC* procedural face, or
131- *          MESH* triangle mesh (vertex index list) or
132- *          SHPE* mathematical shapes like parameterized surfaces
133- *      LBLS* annotation label chunks, can be more (optional)
134- *      ACTN* action chunk(s), animation-pose skeletons, can be more (optional)
135- *          n x m3dfr_t each action contains probably more, but at least one frame
136- *              n x m3dtr_t each frame contains probably more, but at least one transformation
137- *      ASET* inlined asset chunk(s), can be more (optional)
138- *  OMD3 end chunk
139- *
140- * Typical chunks for a game engine: 3DMO, HEAD, CMAP, TMAP, VRTS, BONE, MTRL, MESH, ACTN, OMD3
141- * Typical chunks for CAD software:  3DMO, HEAD, PRVW, CMAP, TMAP, VRTS, MTRL, SHPE, LBLS, OMD3
142- */
